newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan public bodies' rates to fall to 2.9%--MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan public bodies' rates to fall to 2.9%--MOF.

text.p: The lending rates of government-affiliated Japanese financial bodies, such as the Japan Development Bank (JDB), will be cut to 2.9 percent from 3.1 percent, the Finance Ministry (MOF) said on Tuesday.
The decrease will take effect on Wednesday, it said.

Lending rates for the People's Finance Corporation, the Japan Finance Corporation for Small Business, the Hokkaido and Tohoku Development Corporation, the Environmental Sanitation Business Finance Corporation and the Japan Development Bank will also be cut to 2.9 percent, MOF said in a statement.
The decrease in lending rates was due to a decline in Japan's long-term prime rate, a MOF official said.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ) said on Monday it would cut its long-term prime lending rate for June to 2.9 percent, effective June 11, from 3.1 percent in May.
